# Porting parity checklist

The current remaining-feature audit and implementation sequence are in
[PORTING-PLAN.md](PORTING-PLAN.md). This file retains the
historical baseline and chronological verification evidence; baseline-only
missing items must be reconciled with that plan and the later entries below.
Links under `target/verification/` point to the checkout that ran the tests.

This inventory records implementation and acceptance separately. It starts from
Rust commit `f463f9ce2d14d1805d8c5fd170467490ed155427` and the scope in
[HANDOFF.md](HANDOFF.md). **Present** means that the named Rust path exists.
**Partial** identifies a known gap. **Audit** means that a feature-by-feature
comparison is pending. A test target listed as coverage describes an existing
check. A historical result identifies an earlier run. Current acceptance stays
open until a result is recorded for the tested revision and environment. Both
Mosh modes are out of scope. The editor has a reduced native scope with structure
navigation for classes, functions, variables, and placeholders.

## November 23 dialog parity review

Rust implementation `aaa8d037` in [PR #34](https://github.com/chardonnay/korTTY_rust/pull/34)
was compared with Java tag `v2.26.0` (`b235d91f2035`) and the recorded
Windows ARM64 desktop checks.

- **Agent designs.** Activating another module on Standard or Classic already
  creates a custom design. The standalone editor saves the change. A fresh Rust
  process restored the custom default, delay and reduced animations. Java
  appends ` 2` to the preset's full display name and opens a name dialog
  for New, Duplicate and Rename. New opens with `My combination` selected.
  Duplicate selects the proposed name based on the current design. Rust
  generated `Custom design N` and renamed inline at that checkpoint. The
  [naming update](#november-23-agent-design-naming) adds the owned prompts.
  [Java editor](https://github.com/chardonnay/korTTY/blob/v2.26.0/src/main/java/de/kortty/ui/AgentDesignPluginManagerDialog.java)
  · [Rust editor](src/workspace/settings_window/agent_design_settings.rs)
  · [Rust catalog](src/terminal_agent/design/custom.rs)
- **Plan and execution.** At 1,202 by 694 pixels, Java placed Metro above the
  bottom history and Rust placed it below. Java gives the prompt and run
  controls one header above the Plan checklist and execution column. Its
  divider starts at 42% and can be dragged. At this checkpoint the shared
  Rust layout put Metro below the composed pane and used Goal and Activity
  headings and fixed column proportions. The later
  [layout update](#november-23-plan-and-execution-layout) addresses these
  differences. [Java panel](https://github.com/chardonnay/korTTY/blob/v2.26.0/src/main/java/de/kortty/ui/AgentDesignPlanExecution.java)
  · [Rust placement](src/workspace/terminal_agent/design/placement.rs)
  · [Rust panel](src/workspace/terminal_agent/design/plan_execution.rs)
- **Local models.** Both GGUF and MLX have owned Configure windows. The
  GGUF desktop comparison confirmed field order, cancellation and a saved
  context size and idle timeout. The same long path wrapped in Rust. Java
  prompts for copy or reference after the file picker and offers a matching
  runtime when a saved GGUF model requires a different backend. Rust
  embedded import review and offered runtime repair separately at that
  checkpoint. The [GGUF update](#november-23-gguf-import-and-backend-review)
  adds the owned prompts. Java stores the
  Hub publication date for MLX. At this checkpoint Rust's MLX inventory row
  supplied no date. The later [MLX update](#november-23-mlx-publication-date-on-apple-silicon)
  adds that metadata. MLX Configure and the mixed inventory need Apple Silicon

  adds that recovery.

## November 23 Plan and execution layout

The shared terminal and preview layout places Metro before the bottom
Plan and execution panel while retaining the full-width Metro bar beneath
a side timeline. The panel has a prompt and run header, a checklist and
an execution column. The default bottom panel is 152 logical pixels high.
The divider starts at 42% and supports dragging between independently
scrollable columns.

Private automatic launches compared Java v2.26.0 x64 under emulation
and native Rust on the same Windows ARM64 host. The standard dialogs
both captured at 1,202 by 694 pixels. Rust showed the prompt header and
Plan checklist beneath Metro. Dragging the divider after highlighting it
reflowed the answer in the narrower execution column. The compact Rust
dialog captured at 942 by 512 pixels. Scrolling exposed the whole panel
with Close still visible. Side timeline retained the full-width bar.
The divider highlight, panel colors and text spacing still differ from
Java. The native Rust executable had PE machine `0xAA64` and SHA-256
`535503DA10D56BD83E10E0078CE68B9C8CF0ACC00AAB57BDBC9DE66C7619353E`.

Apple Silicon passed four targeted plan tests. The drag fixture verifies
that a native resize event changes the split and that the presenter still
shows the latest typed command output and final answer. Windows ARM64
passed 151 focused cases, including that drag fixture, the shared Metro
positions and bound history-panel approvals. The wider Windows selection
also found a prior Timeline assertion for the old running label. The test
now checks the displayed elapsed time and output line count. The final
source passed Windows ARM64 `cargo check --tests` and nine focused tests
on Apple Silicon, including the corrected Timeline case. A run in the
live desktop terminal with a reviewed command remains open.

## November 23 Agent Design naming

New, Duplicate and Rename open an owned dialog and select the initial
name. New proposes `My combination`. Duplicate and an automatic copy
of a built-in use the full preset name with a numeric suffix starting
at ` 2`. Rename keeps the design ID. Cancel leaves the catalog intact.
The standalone editor saves accepted changes immediately. Global Settings
keeps them in its draft until Save.

The initial Windows ARM64 comparison confirmed the selected New and
Duplicate proposals, Escape and a saved duplicate. The Rust prompt was
taller than Java's. The height constraint was corrected afterward.
The compact prompt and renamed preset after restart still need native
desktop checks. The first Apple Silicon run passed 33 naming and related
dialog tests, including draft behavior, cancellation and stale actions.

## November 23 GGUF import and backend review

The native file picker opens an owned review of the selected GGUF paths.
It reconciles selected shards of the same model, preserves the model purpose
and optional projector controls, and offers private copies or external
references. Eligible detached models retain their reattachment path.
Cancel discards the staged selection. A saved Configure draft that requires
a different backend from the installed runtime offers to open the existing
signed-runtime review or keep the current runtime. Installation requires
the separate review. Windows paths in the model review use their normal
display form while registration retains the canonical source.

The focused Apple Silicon run passed 64 tests serially, including picker
cancellation, batch import, split-model reattachment and both replies to
the runtime offer. Two tests in the earlier parallel run hit the shared
managed-model operation lock. Native desktop acceptance remains open for
both import choices, both runtime responses, and the Configure width and
long-path layout against Java.
[Rust GGUF actions](src/ai_manager/local/managed.rs)

## November 23 Knowledge source outcomes

The source inventory loads each source's last completed outcome and problem
count from private profile metadata. Counts and timestamps for published
passages still come from the index. A source error or an unavailable file
can therefore appear alongside its last successful index. Successful updates
replace the outcome for the reviewed sources. An interrupted batch leaves
the other rows intact. Source and embedding changes invalidate the affected
outcomes. Existing profiles without this metadata continue to show their
index counts and timestamps.

Apple Silicon passed 99 focused tests with six ignored. The manual update
test indexes two sources, fails a later update, then opens a new Manager
and verifies the error, problem count, both saved timestamps and the
other row. Automatic sync also restores an unavailable source, preserving
its published passages. A changed source limit cleared the affected
outcome and preserved the other source's stored problem count. The Windows
ARM64 all-target compilation check passed.
The remaining desktop check covers manual and automatic failures across
a process restart, followed by a successful update of the affected source.
[Source outcome store](src/ai_manager/local/knowledge/outcomes.rs)
· [Source inventory](src/ai_manager/local/knowledge_inventory.rs)
· [Apple Silicon focused tests](target/verification/20261123-source-outcomes-macos-final.log)

## November 23 Complete masked step copy

The selected command step now retains its masked stdout and stderr for
the **Copy output** action. The inline preview keeps its eight-line,
320-character-per-line limit. Copying from an earlier run uses the
retained output of that step and still checks the current run binding,
clipboard policy and credential mask. The separate capture limit for each
stream still applies. The app tests exercise live and retained steps with
different outputs, both streams, a line longer than 32 KiB, and an
additional credential mask. The wider test selection also found that
Metro showed the ongoing response repair as generic analysis. Its active
station now shows the repair status. The final Apple Silicon selection
passed all 125 tests, and the Windows ARM64 all-target compilation check
passed. The native system clipboard exercise remains open.

Normal-design captures measured 982 by 672 pixels for AI Manager and
1202 by 694 pixels for Agent Design on both sides.

In AI Manager, the search kept the General page visible beneath its
results. Selecting the global request timeout by keyboard opened Defaults,

safety page has additional confirmation and runtime message controls.
Its General Internet access page places provider options together.
Continue the comparison of form alignment, profile states and the
remaining primary pages.

## November 22 design editing, command output and settings search

This source comparison uses Java `v2.26.0` (`b235d91f2035`) and the Rust
working tree based on `cb622a66`, including its uncommitted changes.
The [implementation backlog](PORTING-PLAN.md#confirmed-implementation-work)
gives completion checks for each difference.

- **Agent design editor (A2).** Selecting a different module on a Java
  built-in creates and selects a custom copy with that one role changed.
  The default is a separate choice. Java saves committed changes to
  combinations, the default, auto-hide and reduced animations immediately.
  Rust offers module previews on both presets and custom designs. The
  editable role selectors at this checkpoint appeared on custom designs,
  and edits reached storage through the outer Settings save. The subsequent
  [standalone editor and restart checks](#november-23-dialog-parity-review)
  cover automatic copies and immediate persistence. [Java design editor](https://github.com/chardonnay/korTTY/blob/v2.26.0/src/main/java/de/kortty/ui/AgentDesignPluginManagerDialog.java)
  · [Rust design editor](src/workspace/settings_window/agent_design_settings.rs)
  · [Rust Settings draft and save](src/workspace/settings_window.rs)
- **Command step output (A2).** Java's step menu joins the stdout and
  stderr lines already retained for that activity. Rust's inline history
  keeps the last eight combined lines and the first 320 characters of
  each. The step action joins that preview. A successful clipboard test
  with a single short line covers its own case. Long-output verification
  needs markers outside both preview limits and must preserve masking and
  the run's capture limits. [Java step action](https://github.com/chardonnay/korTTY/blob/v2.26.0/src/main/java/de/kortty/ui/AgentRunActions.java)
  · [Java output reader](https://github.com/chardonnay/korTTY/blob/v2.26.0/src/main/java/de/kortty/core/AgentStepReader.java)
  · [Rust step history](src/workspace/terminal_agent/inline_history.rs)
  · [Rust step action](src/workspace/terminal_agent/design/actions.rs)
- **Settings and AI Manager search (D4).** Java uses the same matcher in
  both dialogs. It folds accents, alternate German spellings and
  punctuation, requires every query term to match, ranks labels and pages
  with stable ties, and removes repeated labels on the same page before
  returning up to 40 results. A query matching only the page name can
  reveal that page without listing all its controls. Rust Settings
  already folds accents and requires two characters. AI Manager accepts a
  single character. Both return substring matches in enumeration order.
  The tagged tests include German spelling, punctuation, page-only
  hits, stable ranking and the result limit. Imported GGUF and MLX
  model results already resolve by name, format or registry ID.
  [Java matcher](https://github.com/chardonnay/korTTY/blob/v2.26.0/src/main/java/de/kortty/ui/SettingsSearchMatcher.java)
  · [Java matcher tests](https://github.com/chardonnay/korTTY/blob/v2.26.0/src/test/java/de/kortty/ui/SettingsSearchMatcherTest.java)
  · [Rust Settings search](src/workspace/settings_window.rs)
  · [Rust AI Manager search](src/ai_manager/search.rs)

## Orbit progress and terminal placement

The d15 Orbit status anchors its 72-pixel circle to the terminal's lower
right while keeping the current step label to its left. Opening the list
keeps the circle in place and shows up to twelve recent steps above it,
with the remaining count and existing run and step actions. The ring
eases between progress values over 400 ms. The three dots make a
revolution in 1.6 seconds, hold through a pause, and remain still with
reduced animations. The same presenter is used in Settings. The list
opens from the center of the ring over 340 ms and folds back over 260 ms.
The circular clip follows the current radius as the user reverses the
animation or resizes the pane. During opening, only the visible area
receives pointer input. The list is inert during folding. Reduced
animations shows or hides the entire list immediately. A2 tracks the
remaining native desktop checks.
[Java Orbit presenter](https://github.com/chardonnay/korTTY/blob/v2.26.0/src/main/java/de/kortty/ui/AgentDesignOrbit.java).

the ring and terminal bounds stay fixed. The animation tests cover an
interrupted fill, switching runs, pause and resume, and reduced motion.

passed strict Clippy for the application and its tests.

## Frosted Glass HUD with typed progress

The d04 HUD overlays the lower-right corner of its terminal and shows the
task, current step, typed progress segments and available model usage.
Details opens a typed step list above the card, including the context menu
for each step. Both surfaces leave terminal geometry intact with a history
dock alongside. Run actions are available on the card, and review continues
in the run's Activity window.

The glass samples a bounded region of the rendered terminal at up to ten
frames per second and blurs it behind the tinted card. Keyboard input from
the HUD's own live terminal stream dims the card to 35 percent over 160 ms.
The card restores its opacity after 1.4 seconds of idle time. Reduced
animations makes the opacity changes immediate, uses a steady progress
display and skips the blur. When hidden, the HUD closes its step drawer and
clears the temporary typing fade. On show or reopen, the card fades in over
220 ms and scales from 94 to 100 percent around its center over 240 ms. The
transition repaints without relaying out the terminal and respects reduced
animations. The Settings preview uses the same presenter. A2 tracks native
desktop acceptance.
[Java Frosted Glass HUD](https://github.com/chardonnay/korTTY/blob/v2.26.0/src/main/java/de/kortty/ui/AgentDesignHud.java).

The renderer test checks the blur and tint over terminal pixels, the
rounded corners and the unchanged area outside the card. Iced layout and
pointer tests check placement beside the history dock, stable terminal
geometry and the exact step menu. The typing test covers repeated keys,
idle recovery and reduced motion. The entrance tests check both durations,
centered scaling, replay after hiding, immediate presentation with reduced
motion and intermediate pixels without a layout change. Apple Silicon and
Fedora 44 ARM64 each passed 279 Terminal Agent tests with 12 ignored. Apple
Silicon also passed nine terminal context tests. Strict application Clippy
passed on Apple Silicon and Windows ARM64. Fedora ran in a local container
with its scratch data on a native Linux filesystem.
[Apple Silicon verification](target/verification/20261122-agent-hud-entrance-macos.log)

## Powerline status and step drawer

The d01 Powerline follows Java's bottom placement and segmented status.
It names the running command or latest typed step, then shows the final
answer when available. A specific live phase such as response repair takes
priority over the current step label. The bar counts commands and reports
elapsed time and usage. Its review and run actions use the existing
session-bound controls. Details opens the latest eight typed rows above the bar. A
pending review opens the drawer, and resolution closes it if it was
opened automatically. The drawer grows over 260 ms and the active
spinner changes every 100 ms with animations enabled. Reduced
animations makes the drawer appear immediately and omits the spinner.
The Settings preview and Adaptive Dock's bottom mode share the
Powerline presenter.

On Fedora ARM64 X11, the environment review opened the drawer and
Review focused the existing Agent window. The drawer closed when the
two reviewed loopback requests finished. Manually reopening it copied
the exact selected command output and preserved the 119-column by
31-row grid. The terminal pixels above the bounded drawer were unchanged.
The hide button restored two terminal rows and the View menu restored the
bar with Details closed. The fixture did not verify the configured
keyboard shortcut after a step-menu action. All 72 Terminal Agent design
tests passed on Fedora ARM64. Strict Clippy, including test targets,
passed on Windows ARM64.

history. Command rows show the captured exit code and output line count,
running steps show elapsed seconds, and model rows show reported tokens.
The leading mark animates while a step is running and stays steady with
reduced animations. Narrow rows keep the result on the right while the
step name is clipped. Row actions still resolve the original typed step.

with one retained line, and the reported 20 tokens on the model row in

configured Ctrl+Shift+F7 binding. The initial keyboard fixtures left
the bar visible before and after a step menu action. The hide button
and View menu toggled the bar in both themes. All 73 design tests

## Minimap rail shows typed step previews

The d11 rail reserves fourteen pixels beside the terminal, including when
a history pane occupies the same side. Its colored segments follow the
run's typed steps and keep their order. Hover opens a preview to the left
with the command or step, its result, up to four masked output lines, the
run phase and reported tokens. Reduced animations keeps running segments
steady and opens previews immediately. The Settings preview uses the
same rail and motion rules.

Right-clicking a segment opens the menu bound to that exact step. The
background opens the run menu. An open Minimap menu keeps the rail visible
through its hide deadline, and a changed grid closes the menu. Older
records with text-only activity still open their entry actions. A2 tracks
the interactive desktop acceptance of the redesigned rail.

Clippy passed on Apple Silicon and Windows ARM64.

## Context sent with a reviewed Terminal Agent request

**Sent along** lists the latest confirmed nonempty model turn's masked
organization, global and connection memory, approved reference excerpts,
and included skills. It distinguishes pinned and automatic skills, marks
partial reference excerpts and shows estimated tokens. The shared popup
opens from the terminal footer or the run's Activity view. A draft or a
failed pre-dispatch review does not publish a receipt. An empty turn keeps
the previous receipt. The receipt is held with its own run and is masked
again when retained alongside the finished history.

Interactive live terminal requests can include eligible, previously
approved reference files in the exact model review. The dispatch guard
revalidates the selected references and the memory policy. Private runs
still exclude personal memory and reference files. Interactive desktop
acceptance remains under A2.

that a change after review prevents dispatch and publication. Both suites
verify the memory and skill receipt and rejection of a stale skill review.
The Fedora run uses a local Fedora 44 ARM64 container with a local

## Command review in the other Agent histories

The side timeline places the pending command beside the newest node.
Plan and Execution displays it in the execution column. Card Stack
shows it as the front card after the preceding activity, and Log Table
places its controls in a fixed section above the scrolling table. The
current command is bound to its run, terminal, focus and execution
policy. Attached and detached picture-in-picture histories use the
same checks. When a cursor suggestion owns the review, its binding
controls the numeric keys.
[Java history-panel behavior](https://github.com/chardonnay/korTTY/blob/v2.26.0/app-docs/site/docs/en/features/ai-agent-designs.md#history-panels).

controls, repeated keys, a policy change after the decision was
queued, and cancellation through the visible card. Windows ARM64 and
Apple Silicon both passed 261 Terminal Agent tests and nine terminal
context tests. Four Windows and twelve Apple Silicon fixture tests
stayed ignored. App Clippy passed with warnings denied on Apple Silicon.
Live desktop acceptance remains open for these panels.

## Plan and Execution uses typed command results

The Plan and Execution design shows typed steps with status marks. The
execution column follows the newest command while the agent works. It
shows the running state or exit code, elapsed time and up to five lines
from the masked output tail. Its context menu acts on that exact command
even if later model or question steps arrive. A pending approval takes
priority. A completed run displays its final answer in the same column.
Saved activity without typed steps uses its existing text view.

Progress changes animate over 360 milliseconds. Reduced animations show
the new progress immediately and keep the running indicator still.
Completed commands and answered questions draw a check mark over 320
milliseconds. The presenter keeps the first completion time for each
step. Reduced animations and reopened history show the complete mark
immediately. The Settings preview uses the same renderer and refresh
timing. Native desktop acceptance remains open.

## November 21 Numeric decisions in Terminal Agent cursor approval

The d14 hint follows the same run-wide approval conditions as the
Activity window. Both use the existing ordinary-command approval and
its saved-policy and profile checks. Either Enter or 1 approves the
displayed command once. When broader approval is available, 2 approves
the remaining ordinary commands and 3 dismisses the current review.
Under per-command confirmation, 2 dismisses and 3 is consumed without
changing the review. An event retains the action shown when the key
was captured. Dispatch rechecks it against the current review and
policy so a stale dismissal key cannot become an approval.

The private Fedora X11 session verified a single press of 2 produced
both expected stdout lines once. A separate run used 3 to dismiss.
With confirmation required on every command, 3 left the review and
the visible shell bytes unchanged, 1 ran the first command, and 2
dismissed the second. The transcript contained only the first stdout
line. The native widget test covers the digit row and numpad cases,
and the workspace test changes policy between capture and dispatch.
Fedora ARM64 and Apple Silicon each passed 27 cursor, preview, and
run-wide approval tests. Windows ARM64 passed strict Clippy.

## November 21 Terminal Agent Standard design

Standard combines d03 in-terminal blocks, the d08 Metro line, approval
in history and a fixed arrangement. A valid connection choice takes
precedence over the global default. Missing and unrecognized roles in
custom designs independently inherit the corresponding Standard module.
Explicitly saved transcript and step-strip modules retain their existing
IDs. Classic and Floating retain their layouts. Metro shows a `+N` badge
for additional unfinished runs on the same stream with the same status
and history panel. Paused runs contribute to the count. This checkpoint
allowed up to five unfinished Ask requests, each with a separate review.
Inline keyboard actions bind to the rendered block closest to the prompt.

the surviving request produced one loopback call. Selecting its result
in the run picker showed the completed rail with 20 reported tokens.

five-request limit. Windows ARM64 passed application and test-target

## November 21 Overlapping Terminal Agent runs

A pane accepts up to five standalone Run, Ask and Planning runs on its
current stream. Each run owns its reviews, results and cancellation.
Environment probes, ordinary commands and sudo operations use the same
per-pane execution slot through worker completion. During contention a
command stays in review with a fresh epoch and any automatic approval for
that run is revoked. Saved Swarm routes retain their existing ownership
checks. Choosing a hosted-only Planning or Agent run opens its own tab
while the visible terminal status stays attached to its source run.

In a private Fedora Wayland session, Run, Ask and Planning each reached
review from one local Bash pane. The run picker opened the Planning tab.
Returning to the terminal showed the same pending Run probe. Approving
that probe recorded its output in Run and opened a separate model review.
Approving Ask produced one loopback request and its answer while the Run
and Planning model requests stayed pending.

The native workspace suites passed 4,830 tests on Fedora and 4,786 on
Apple Silicon. The first Apple Silicon run hit a transient busy lock in
the Snippet Analysis export test. The unchanged rerun passed. The
concurrency regressions cover the shared cap, fresh review after a
contended probe, cancellation, and invalidation on stream replacement.
Fedora and Windows ARM64 passed application and test-target Clippy with
warnings denied.
[Java run limit](https://github.com/chardonnay/korTTY/blob/v2.26.0/src/main/java/de/kortty/ui/MainWindow.java)

· [Apple Silicon suite](target/verification/20261121-agent-mixed-macos-retry.log)
· [Windows ARM64 Clippy](target/verification/20261121-agent-mixed-windows.log).

The Fedora ARM64 Wayland desktop accepted the typed Run, Ask, and

as a group over 250 ms and releases its layout space at the end. Reduced
animations removes the status at the deadline. Zero seconds keeps it
visible. A manual hide takes effect immediately, and restoring a finished
status through the Agent Panel keeps it visible.

composited frames before the terminal recovered its space. The same
three-second delay with reduced animations went directly from the steady

zero setting and manual restoration. Fourteen targeted Apple Silicon
tests passed for the timing, compositing, clipping and Settings preview.
Windows ARM64 targeted Clippy passed with warnings denied. Repeat the
native desktop checks for the other status designs and platforms.

## November 21 Real OpenSSH sudo/PAM for the Terminal Agent

Fedora ARM64 verified the accepted-plan preflight over a pinned OpenSSH
connection with system sudo and PAM. A private loopback server used a
synthetic login and isolated sudo policy and timestamps. The direct
transport and the native Landlock-confined worker each rejected a wrong
vault password. Both requested a fresh approval for the retry and reached
model review after successful authentication. The separately approved
command reused the run's authenticated PTY and wrote receipts with
effective UID and file-owner UID zero in the reviewed directory. The model
received no implementation request before authentication, and the
receipts did not exist before command approval.

Fedora ARM64 passed 228 selected application tests and both opt-in real
PAM tests. Apple Silicon passed 227 selected application tests and the
separate OpenSSH test with simulated sudo. Native macOS system sudo
acceptance remains open.

A standalone run can offer manual sudo authentication on its reviewed

elevated command requires its own approval.

inside a disposable Flatpak build used the actual host D-Bus service and a
simulated sudo challenge. It verified that the reviewed shared directory
could receive the challenge and accept command input after authentication.

password, and that cancelling a challenge closed the private host process.

the actual Flatpak host service. The fixture ran as a synthetic account
with a private filesystem, PAM configuration and sudo timestamps. The
wrong password was rejected. The correct password authenticated the
private PTY. A separately approved command reused that PTY without
another prompt and wrote a root-owned result in the reviewed directory.

## November 20 Terminal Agent run presentation

AI Manager saves the default presentation for newly opened interactive Run.
The Chat tab hosts the existing reviewed Agent flow, preserves the original
terminal stream and cancels its owned operation on close. Finished runs keep
their presentation when reopened from history. Java restore fills an unset
preference and reports unknown values. The native desktop review and the
accepted-plan entry point are tracked under A2.

## November 20 Terminal Agent Log Table

Design 16 renders the retained and masked typed steps as a sortable table.
It shows local time, activity kind, step, result or exit code, elapsed
time, and reported tokens. Unknown values display a dash. The answer
stays at the bottom when the step rows are sorted. Double-clicking a
row opens that step's retained output or the final answer. Right-clicking
a step reveals the existing step actions in its details. Both the
live panel and the Settings preview use the same table.

The Apple Silicon run passed all 61 selected Agent designs, Settings
preview and history tests. The new regressions exercise native Iced
double-click delivery and verify that sorting and eviction preserve
the identity of the selected output. Strict workspace Clippy passed
on Windows ARM64.

· [Windows ARM64 Clippy](target/verification/20261120-agent-log-table-windows-clippy-final.log)

The table uses the theme accent for a 900 ms flash when a step or answer
first appears. The running marker advances every 120 ms. Sorting and
updates to an existing row preserve its first appearance time. Pausing
the run keeps the marker still. Reduced animations also suppresses the
flash. Native desktop acceptance remains under A2.

## November 20 Hub MLX pause, resume and discard

The MLX transfer saves a private receipt with the reviewed manifest and
its last verified checkpoint. The browser can find it after restart,
display the package for review, and resume or discard it. Resume checks
completed assets and the saved prefix. Byte-range requests require the
original strong ETag and the exact remaining range. The complete package
still passes native validation before registry publication. Cancelled
transfers and explicit discard clean up the owned stage.

On Apple Silicon, an anonymous live Hub test reviewed eight assets for
`mlx-community/SmolLM2-135M-Instruct-8bit` at commit
`0f0d9b8218915bc34d401e1a340b8c049d300d5e`. It paused after downloading
5,318,229 bytes, read the saved receipt, and resumed with a fresh Hub client.
The native registry published all 147,874,605 verified bytes and the transfer
removed its checkpoint. Interactive Mac acceptance remains under B4.
[Rust MLX Hub transfer](src/local_ai/managed_models/huggingface/mlx/download.rs)
· [Apple Silicon live Hub test](target/verification/20261120-mlx-hub-resume-macos-live.log)

package. The review shows the immutable commit, all supported native
assets, individual sizes and SHA-256 digests. LFS assets use the Hub's
published SHA-256. For ordinary Git metadata the review verifies the
commit-pinned content against its Git object identity and computes its
SHA-256. The download will use this manifest. A changed selection,
search or vault revision invalidates an in-flight review.

detected RAM. Show all models includes unknown and oversized results. An
explicit search or Load More can start up to four concurrent metadata
lookups to determine the smallest complete downloadable weight set. Rows
update as replies arrive. The browser displays the visible and filtered
counts while checking sizes. Search and access changes cancel the previous
lookups, and saved-token lookups use the search's vault revision. Download
actions require a separate immutable artifact review.

## November 20 Java OS symbol assignments

Java backups contain custom symbol IDs, names and original image filenames.
For imported connections, Rust records that metadata as a pending
assignment. A local custom symbol with the same ID requires the same
explicit review as any other candidate. Missing or ambiguous metadata
falls back to the imported ID. The source filename is display metadata.
Built-in symbols transfer directly.

In Connection Manager, select the restored connection and review its
imported symbol. Use **Manage symbols…** to add an image when needed, then
choose a local symbol in the connection's **OS symbol** picker. The picker
rechecks the selected local image before committing the assignment.
Selecting **No symbol** dismisses the suggestion. A replay of the same
backup preserves the reviewed assignment.

## November 20 SFTP transfer part cleanup

**Remove transfer parts…** reviews regular `*.kortty-part` files in the
folder shown on either side. Cleanup has a preview with the exact names
and a separate confirmation. The Local pane can work without an SSH
connection. The Server pane binds the review to its existing connection
and uses a protected quarantine to check the exact object before removal.
The app reserves active flat stages across its SFTP workers and checks the
reservation again at removal. Other SFTP clients cannot share these
reservations and must finish writing before cleanup is confirmed. Links,
folders and backup files are excluded. Native durable checkpoints retain
their separate queue and receipt workflow. A changed or newly active entry
is kept, other reviewed parts can still be removed, and the pane refreshes
after the batch.

## November 20 Logfile Manager folder discovery

The catalogue scans existing log folders from saved SSH connections before
their first logging session, including connections with capture disabled.
It merges configured, manually added and logger-discovered folders by
canonical path. Only exclusively manual folders can be forgotten. Older
Rust registries stored both origins in `folders`; those entries retain
manual status until a saved connection or a later capture establishes
another origin. Forgetting removes the registry entry and preserves the
logs. Native desktop acceptance is open.

### Spotlight entry and submission

Spotlight fades in over 140 ms and scales from 96% over 160 ms. When a
direct submission starts a run with a Spotlight pill, the card fades and
shrinks toward the pill over 420 ms. Submission into the separate setup, or
a run with another status, fades over 220 ms. The departing card has no
prompt, history or input controls. Closing with Escape is immediate. Pane
changes, loss of eligibility and reduced motion discard the departing card.
The Settings replay uses the same motion with the sample prompt.
[Java Spotlight](https://github.com/chardonnay/korTTY/blob/v2.26.0/src/main/java/de/kortty/ui/AgentDesignSpotlight.java)

entry into review, focus release, stale submit rejection and cancellation of
the departure on privacy and motion preference changes.

### Toast transitions and finished-run retention

The Toast status and Settings preview share a clipped slide-in and fade.
Ordinary notices enter over 260 ms, count down for four seconds, fade over
220 ms and collapse over 160 ms. Pending review slides into view and stays
available through the existing review action. Reduced motion uses a static
notice for four seconds and leaves pending review visible.

## Java terminal Agent prompt history

The Java v2.26.0 profile preview lists masked
`terminalAgentInputHistory` entries and the proposed history limit. The
import preserves the prompt text after masking, its original timestamp
and the archive's order. Java stores prompt and timestamp without a
mode. Rust labels the restored entries as imported. Composer selection
and shell alias completion can recall those entries for review.

Startup restore appends distinct prompts to available slots in an existing
native history. Its local ordering, entries and limit take precedence.
A new store adopts the Java limit with the existing 5–100 bounds and
20-entry default. Native encrypted backups also carry this private store.
Private sessions have no access to it. The terminal Tab history chooser
uses Java's 460 × 260 defaults and width and height limits. Resize grips
on the top and right edges save changes in the profile when released.
Small splits constrain the displayed size while preserving the profile
preferences. Java backup restore imports each dimension into its unset
native field. The composer offers entry removal and confirmed clearing.
The November 20 changes also add these actions to the terminal Tab chooser.
Verify interactive recall, deletion, clearing and resizing on native desktops.

## Manual question history

The audit compared Java tag `v2.26.0` (`b235d91f2035`) with the Rust working

## Porting continuation on 2026-11-18

### SFTP hidden entries

The SFTP Manager stores local and server visibility separately. Java
backup values fill unset fields. New standalone, attached and project
views inherit the preferences. Incognito views keep changes in memory.
The Java visibility shortcut now routes to the focused file listing.
Native desktop interaction and restart checks remain open.

Apple Silicon passed 37 backup merge, SFTP and project file-view tests.
Windows ARM64 application and test-target Clippy passed with warnings
denied for project code.
[Apple Silicon](target/verification/20261118-sftp-hidden-macos.log)
and [Windows](target/verification/20261118-sftp-hidden-windows.log).

The Apple Silicon shortcut checkpoint passed eight tests. The widget
fixture switched between both lists and checked focus loss, repeated
keys, and extra modifiers. Windows ARM64 application and test-target
Clippy passed with warnings denied for project code.
[Apple Silicon](target/verification/20261118-sftp-hidden-shortcut-macos-final.log)
and [Windows](target/verification/20261118-sftp-hidden-shortcut-windows-final.log).

The SFTP path shortcut focuses and selects the current path in the
active pane. The widget fixture replaced the highlighted path in each
pane, starting from a list click or focus in a filter field. Changing
the server route retains that pane's hidden-file toggle. Apple Silicon
passed 12 SFTP and project file-view tests. Windows ARM64 application
and test-target Clippy passed with warnings denied for project code.
[Apple Silicon](target/verification/20261118-sftp-path-shortcut-macos.log)
and [Windows](target/verification/20261118-sftp-path-shortcut-windows.log).

The focused list handles F2, Delete and Command/Ctrl+Backspace through
the existing single-entry dialogs. The tests exercise both pane targets,
selection checks and the confirmation boundary. Apple Silicon passed
14 SFTP and project file-view tests. Windows ARM64 application and
test-target Clippy passed with warnings denied for project code.
Native keyboard acceptance and Java's multi-entry recursive deletion
remain open.
[Apple Silicon](target/verification/20261118-sftp-file-shortcuts-macos.log)
and [Windows](target/verification/20261118-sftp-file-shortcuts-windows.log).

Delete now accepts multiple entries from one SFTP pane. The confirmation
lists the directory and selected names. The worker checks each name,
kind and available size before the first deletion. It stops on an error
and reports how many entries were removed. Empty folders and links are
handled without recursive traversal. Apple Silicon passed ten focused
tests, including a local fixture where one changed entry prevented the
whole selection from being deleted. Windows ARM64 application and
test-target Clippy passed with warnings denied for project code.
Live server and desktop acceptance, nonempty folder deletion and
cancellation during deletion remain open.
[Apple Silicon](target/verification/20261118-sftp-batch-delete-macos.log)
and [Windows](target/verification/20261118-sftp-batch-delete-windows.log).

The SFTP delete workflow now supports stopping a running selection and
asks before closing a view with a deletion in progress. A local fixture
stopped before any removal and after one confirmed removal. A protocol
fixture lost the reply to a server removal and verified that the
confirmed count excludes that entry and reports its uncertain outcome.
Apple Silicon passed 12 focused tests. Windows ARM64 application and
test-target Clippy passed with warnings denied for project code. Exact
recursive review and removal, native desktop interaction and live
server acceptance remain open.
[Apple Silicon](target/verification/20261118-sftp-delete-cancel-macos.log)
and [Windows](target/verification/20261118-sftp-delete-cancel-windows.log).

The SFTP Manager can preview and delete nonempty trees of regular files
and folders. Apply consumes one review on the same worker, compares the
current tree, and uses the existing reviewed removals in child-first
order. A native fixture checked the descendant preview, rejection after
an added file, preservation of an unselected sibling, successful removal
and replay rejection. Seven Apple Silicon tests and Windows ARM64
application and test-target Clippy passed. Recursive link and special
entries, other server targets and live desktop/server acceptance remain
open.
[Apple Silicon](target/verification/20261118-sftp-recursive-delete-macos.log)
and [Windows](target/verification/20261118-sftp-recursive-delete-windows.log).

A native Apple Silicon OpenSSH SFTP subsystem fixture exercised the
SFTP Manager's review and confirmation events over pipes. The first
review became stale after a file appeared and both files remained.
A fresh review removed the four selected tree entries, refreshed the
server pane, kept the unselected sibling and left no quarantine behind.
The existing native reviewed synchronization removal test also passed.
[Apple Silicon OpenSSH](target/verification/20261118-sftp-recursive-openssh-macos.log).

A second native Apple Silicon test exercised the regular SFTP Manager
worker over loopback OpenSSH using public-key authentication and a pinned
host key. A file added after review caused the worker to refuse deletion
and preserve both files. A fresh review removed exactly four entries,
refreshed the listing with the unselected sibling, and left no quarantine
directory. The worker and SSH subprocess exited. The passing run used
a private directory under the test account's home with OpenSSH
`StrictModes` enabled. Native desktop input and other server routes
remain open.
[Authenticated Apple Silicon OpenSSH](target/verification/20261118-sftp-recursive-pinned-macos-final.log).

Recursive server deletion now reviews symbolic links with SFTP
`LSTAT` and `READLINK`. The review binds the stored target bytes. The

quarantine. The authenticated Apple Silicon OpenSSH fixture refused a
changed link target, then removed a dangling link, a directory link and
a separately selected link in a fresh review of seven entries. Both
unselected targets remained intact.
[Apple Silicon OpenSSH link removal](target/verification/20261118-sftp-recursive-links-macos.log).

Recursive server deletion also reviews recognized POSIX special entries
inside selected folders. The worker checks their type and metadata and

Apple Silicon OpenSSH repeat refused a FIFO replaced by a regular file

control excluded a separately marked special entry. The native fixture
did not exercise device nodes.
Windows ARM64 test-target Clippy passed.

and [Windows ARM64 Clippy](target/verification/20261118-sftp-recursive-special-windows.log).

The SFTP Manager now accepts recognized server special entries in a
mixed selection for reviewed deletion. Transfer buttons and pointer drag

the FIFO with a folder and a link, refused a stale review after the FIFO
became a regular file, and removed nine entries after a fresh review.
Windows ARM64 test-target Clippy passed. Native desktop interaction
remains open.

and [Windows ARM64 Clippy](target/verification/20261118-sftp-recursive-mixed-windows.log).

Unix local recursive deletion now reviews symbolic links and recognized
special entries using descriptor-relative, no-follow metadata. The

The unselected link target remained intact. A separate test cancelled

[Apple Silicon tests](target/verification/20261118-sftp-recursive-local-macos-final.log)
and [Windows ARM64 Clippy](target/verification/20261118-sftp-recursive-local-windows.log).

[Windows ARM64 runtime](target/verification/20261118-sftp-recursive-junctions-windows.log),

### SFTP comparison AI font size

The AI panel in the file comparison now adjusts question, streaming
response and finished answer text from 9 to 32 points, with a 13-point
default. Ordinary views save the setting for reopening. Incognito
changes remain in the current view. Java `sftpDiffAiFontSize` fills
the unset native preference and clamps the saved integer as in the
Java dialog. The encrypted Java-backup fixture verified restore and
preservation of a subsequent native choice on additive replay. The
Apple Silicon file-comparison, SFTP preference and restore groups passed
with the packaged-app fixture ignored. Windows ARM64 test-target Clippy
passed. Native desktop interaction remains open.
[Apple Silicon tests](target/verification/20261118-sftp-ai-font-macos-verified.log)
and [Windows ARM64 Clippy](target/verification/20261118-sftp-ai-font-windows.log).

### Java guide zoom

The Java backup reader imports `guideFontScalePercent` into the native
Manual even when Java's separate application font scale is automatic.
The value clamps to the Java and native reader range of 70–250%. Existing
native zoom takes precedence. Backups that lack the guide field retain
the earlier compatibility fallback from an explicitly saved manual UI
scale. Malformed and duplicate guide fields are reported as omissions.
Apple Silicon passed 57 focused tests across guide import, Manual
behavior and backup restore, with the packaged-app fixture ignored.
Windows ARM64 test-target Clippy passed. Native desktop reopening remains
open.
[Apple Silicon tests](target/verification/20261118-java-guide-zoom-macos.log)
and [Windows ARM64 Clippy](target/verification/20261118-java-guide-zoom-windows.log).

### Java ASCII Art preview zoom

Java backup restore reads `asciiArtPreviewFontSize` as a fractional
size. Finite values clamp to Java's 6–40 range. Invalid values are
reported as omissions. The ASCII Art window applies the imported size
when its native preferences have no saved zoom. Existing integer zoom
values remain readable, and the native preview and zoom controls use the
effective size. [Fedora ARM64](target/verification/20261118-java-ascii-art-zoom-fedora.log)
passed 18 backup-data tests and 16 ASCII Art tests.
[Windows ARM64](target/verification/20261118-java-ascii-art-zoom-windows.log)
passed application and test-target Clippy. Live dialog acceptance remains open.

### Remembered snippet translation language

The snippet assistant prefills the last translation language when it opens.
A valid translation review remembers the choice without sending the
request. The request preview includes the language only for translation.
Java `snippetTranslationTargetLanguage` fills an unset preference and
keeps valid Unicode names. Saved native choices take precedence.
[Fedora ARM64](target/verification/20261118-snippet-translation-fedora.log)
passed 33 focused backup, request and assistant tests.
[Windows ARM64 application and test-target Clippy](target/verification/20261118-snippet-translation-windows.log)
passed. Native editor and restart acceptance remain open.

### Selectable snippet alternatives

Snippet assistance requests structured code alternatives for the marked
selection or the complete snippet. The returned candidates are bounded
and deduplicated. A candidate opens a diff and can replace the reviewed
range through the normal Apply action. The existing source revision,
masking, placeholder and Undo checks apply. The Snippet Editor setting
accepts 1–10 alternatives and defaults to three. Java backup restore
fills an unset value from `aiSnippetAlternativeSolutionCount`.
[Fedora ARM64](target/verification/20261118-snippet-alternatives-fedora.log)
passed 35 focused backup, candidate and assistant tests.
[Windows ARM64 Clippy](target/verification/20261118-snippet-alternatives-windows.log)
passed for the app and test targets. The interactive workflow with a
configured provider remains open.

### AI comparison summary divider

Snippet alternatives, migration results and staged snippet or folder
proposals can resize the scrollable summary above the source comparison.
The initial height estimates the summary content and reserves space for
the comparison. The app stores the relative position after a drag and
shares it across supported review surfaces. Java restore fills an unset
value from `aiDiffDialogSummaryDividerPosition`. A saved native position
takes precedence. Windows ARM64 passed 252 tests with two ignored,
including compact-height bounds, drag completion, import clamping and
additive replay. Native desktop drag, resize and reopen acceptance
remains open.
[Windows verification](target/verification/20261119-ai-diff-summary-windows.log)

### Snippet library column widths

The native library displays name, language, category, operating system,
tags and the effective export executable state in separate columns.
Each header has its own resize grip. The table scrolls horizontally
and keeps its header visible while the rows scroll vertically. The
workspace preserves single and multi-selection, context actions,
opening and drag operations on the row. A completed drag saves its
column width. Java restore fills matching unset widths from
`snippetManagerColumnWidths`. Windows ARM64 passed 278 tests with two
ignored. The native layout test aligned the header and rows inside a
260-point viewport with horizontal overflow. The backup and state tests
covered duplicate fields, native precedence, bounds and drag completion.
[Windows verification](target/verification/20261119-snippet-columns-windows-final.log)

The Favorite column toggles a persisted per-snippet flag. Private Java
library imports keep the flag and both timestamps. The Modified column
shows the last modification or creation time in UTC. The Lines column
follows Java line counting for CR, LF and CRLF. A trailing delimiter
does not add a line.
Java backup restore also accepts the widths for these three columns.
The Windows ARM64 focused suite passed 383 tests with two HTTPS
fixture tests ignored. Coverage includes favorite persistence, the
Java library import, line counting, column widths and table layout.
Desktop interaction stays open.
[Windows verification](target/verification/20261119-snippet-library-stats-windows.log)

The Uses column displays the persisted count. Private Java imports keep
the count and last-used timestamp, and Java window restore accepts the
column width. The native count advances when a resolved saved snippet
is copied or a terminal session accepts its input. Incognito terminal
sends leave the count untouched. The store applies the increment to the
current library under the write lock. Usage updates leave the reviewed
source and modification timestamp intact.
The Windows ARM64 focused suite passed 385 tests with two HTTPS
fixture tests ignored. Coverage includes Java usage import, width
restore, usage persistence and policy-aware copy. The updated Unix PTY
test asserts a single increment after a confirmed send. It awaits a
native Unix run.
[Windows verification](target/verification/20261119-snippet-usage-windows.log)

The table starts with favorites first and higher usage first within each
group. Rows with equal priority remain alphabetical. Clicking a header
cycles that column through ascending, descending and default order.
A usage refresh keeps the visible rows in place under the default order.
The toolbar and row context menu toggle the marked snippets in one write.
The per-row star still toggles only its own snippet. Selection is tracked
by snippet ID through sort and refresh operations.

### Insert a saved snippet into a file editor

The Snippet Manager offers Insert into editor from the saved snippet
actions and the library context menu. It resolves the same variables
and built-ins as Copy resolved and binds the chosen editor before any
prompt. It targets file editor tabs in the associated main window or
native editors opened through that window. The normal writable editor
route inserts at the caret, converts line endings to the current
preference and preserves the insertion as a single undo step. The first
unescaped `${cursor}` positions the caret after expansion. Usage advances
after a successful insertion. Interactive desktop focus transfer remains
open for acceptance.
The Windows ARM64 rerun passed 428 tests across the editor, Snippet
Manager, Scheduler and Teamwork. It covered the editor binding when
focus changes during variable review and the Teamwork Scheduler
round-trip with group membership and host-pin checks. Eight tests were
ignored. They require a loopback Git daemon, native formatter or
compiler tools, or a disposable Windows OpenSSH SFTP fixture.
[Windows verification](target/verification/20261119-teamwork-editor-windows.log)

### Run a saved snippet with positional arguments

The native library offers ordinary and parameterized terminal actions.
The parameter dialog prefills declared variables and accepts one
positional argument per nonblank line. The POSIX command quotes each
argument independently, including spaces and literal apostrophes. Bash,
Python, Perl and Ruby use the same pinned terminal route as the command
palette, with source and variable revalidation and any required paste
review. The action keeps the existing one-line input limit and rejects
terminal control characters in arguments. Incognito
runs leave usage and default values unchanged. The native desktop dialog
and delivery to a POSIX shell and an SSH pane remain open for acceptance.
The Windows ARM64 focused suite passed 296 tests with two HTTPS fixture
tests ignored. Coverage includes literal argument quoting, the input
limit, prefilled defaults, target selection and cancellation.
[Windows verification](target/verification/20261119-snippet-terminal-parameters-windows.log)

### Wayland text drops in terminal panes

Native Wayland accepts copy-only UTF-8 text offers up to 64 KiB. An
offer containing file URIs keeps the existing file route. The terminal
resolves the text target through the pane bounds at the drop point,
then binds the paste to that pane and stream generation. The usual paste
protection applies. Managed internal clipboard, mirrored input, modal
state and unavailable targets reject the drop. Java
`terminalDragDropEnabled` fills the unset native setting.

passed for target hit testing, paste protection and encrypted Java
restore. The first build hit a GNU ld ARM64 relocation overflow. The
successful run temporarily staged signed Fedora LLVM lld packages.
[Windows ARM64 Clippy](target/verification/20261118-wayland-text-drop-windows.log)
passed for the app and test targets. Live Wayland compositor testing
and other desktop text backends remain open.

Native Wayland file offers can open an SFTP upload review on the SSH
split they hit. The separate SFTP channel resolves the tracked shell
directory or uses its start directory. The review shows the canonical
destination before any upload. The stream, shell context and transfer
policy stay bound to the upload through completion. The dialog uses the
existing queue and conflict controls. Closing it stops its channel.

passed for the app and test targets. Live Wayland drag gestures remain open.

### Recurring protected folder creation and confirmed receiver progression

Calendar and Chain approval can now start at a reviewed absent protected folder
in either direction and sudo mode. The first firing publishes one complete
private tree with no replacement of an intervening destination. Successful
completion advances the device-local grant from its reviewed vacancy to the
confirmed created receiver. Subsequent runs use the existing-folder merge path
and must match that receiver. Source bytes may change within the reviewed scope
and firing limits; a separately created or replaced root is never adopted.

The approval index preserves the creation phase, pending firing and confirmed
successor across reopen. A zero, unchanged-vacancy, wrong-firing or stale-worker
completion cannot advance it. Pending creation blocks further automatic runs
until explicit reapproval. After progression, a merge can confirm only the same
receiver. Approval duration, consumed firings, Calendar/Chain cutoffs, action and
payload limits, current route, pins, groups, sudo policy and revocation checks
remain in force. The root creation counts as an action even for an empty source.

Uploads use an explicit `create_root` opt-in in the fixed Rust folder helper.
Legacy requests omit the field and retain their previous wire shape and merge
behavior. Creation requires a receiver receipt, a currently permitted parent,
a bound vacancy and privately verified complete payloads. It publishes the root
once, then confirms the same held receiver through its public name before
returning a successor. The receipt uses the same policy/path/metadata/birth
identity contract as subsequent protected merges. A root publication that cannot
be fully confirmed retains the pending device-local state.

Downloads bind the parent and vacant name before requesting source payloads.
They verify every digest and the final source acknowledgement before local
publication. The destination vacancy and current grant are rechecked at each
publication attempt, including Windows retries. The returned receipt must match
both the staged root and the published receiver. Local creation and existing
merges share the same receiver identity representation. Filesystems without
stable directory birth identity remain ineligible for recurring approval.

The form retains the reviewed creation/merge choice and recurring limits across
reopen, and discloses that later runs may replace eligible files while keeping
recovery originals. The Scheduler fixture covers sixteen combinations of
direction, sudo mode, initial receiver phase and optional Calendar with Chain.
It verifies actual predecessor admission, rejection of a forged trigger, sudo
scope changes, reopen and the persisted transition to the confirmed receiver.

Live pinned SSH execution through the installed updated helper, actual vault
interaction, configured native Scheduler review/recovery and updated release
packages remain open. This does not close T3/Q1/Q2 or the overall porting goal.

### Recurring protected folder merges into existing receivers

The receiver-witness groundwork is now connected to Calendar and Chain approval
for existing protected folder receivers, in upload and download directions and
with passwordless or separately provisioned vault-backed sudo. The form retains
recurring limits across reopen and offers the option only for an existing-folder
merge. Ordinary SFTP source changes keep their earlier preference behavior.
Protected scope binds the selected route, paths, direction, excludes, schedule,
predecessors/freshness, time zone, limits and sudo mode. Manual/cascade starts do
not reuse a recurring grant, and the runtime checks the actual active firing.

The device-local approval index has a separate protected-tree state; ordinary
SFTP and protected single-file receipts cannot be reused as tree authority.
A matching receiver and bounded action/payload claim is persisted before any
publication. It consumes the firing allowance and records an outstanding run.
Only a complete, confirmed merge with the same receiver clears that state.
Uncertain/failed publication or process interruption leaves it pending across
reopen, blocking later automatic publication until explicit reapproval. New
approval invalidates old workers while retaining calendar and Chain cutoffs.
Existing per-entry recovery copies remain available in the reported locations.

Download preview and claim limits include all source payload streamed by the
helper, including unchanged files. Reapproval, pins, route membership, current
policy and receipt state are rechecked at publication. A published batch whose
completion cannot be persisted is reported as requiring a new receiver review.
The managed and credential checks remain independent of the standing grant.

### Protected folder receiver receipts: recurring-transfer groundwork

The protected tree-merge protocol now has an explicitly requested receiver
receipt. Without that request, the request, review and completion JSON retain
the legacy field shape. A requested receipt must be present and nonzero before
the client accepts the review. The Linux helper binds it to its policy revision
and the held root directory's path, identity, mount, birth time, ownership,
permissions and extended attributes, using the existing descriptor checks.
It confirms the same receipt only after every publication and a final scope
check. The client also requires a matching completion and successful helper exit.
An uncertain or partially completed merge never produces a success receipt.

Local protected downloads derive a corresponding receiver witness from the
reviewed root metadata and native birth identity. Platforms/filesystems without
that identity retain one-use behavior but cannot provide this durable witness.
Per-entry content proofs and race checks remain separate: legitimate payload
changes do not change the root witness, while a replaced root does. Download
publication returns the witness only after the full merge and final directory
checks, retaining the existing recovery behavior.

The internal pre-transfer claim now carries the exact proof, optional receiver,
action count and payload bytes. Protected downloads charge the complete streamed
manifest, including unchanged files, because the existing helper streams them.
Uploads charge the changed payload that the helper actually receives.

At this checkpoint the work was groundwork, and validation still rejected
recurring privileged copies. The later existing-receiver entry connects this
protocol to scoped Scheduler approval and execution. Persistent per-firing
admission, pending/completed receipt state, failure recovery, calendar/Chain and
sudo-mode binding, existing/vacant receiver progression in both directions,
the native review/limits UI, and live helper acceptance still need to be connected
and verified. Current one-use approvals remain in place.
Targeted verification passed on native Apple Silicon and Fedora ARM64. Both
passed the three merge protocol tests, three local protected-folder tests and
18 Scheduler sync tests. The broader privileged selection passed 30 tests on
each platform (one ignored on macOS, 46 on Fedora). The focused protected-folder
selection had two additional ignored Linux cases. Fedora also passed the new
server-binary receiver-anchor test with real directory and file changes; that
Linux-only code is absent on macOS. A separate scheduled-prefix selection
matched no tests and is not counted as coverage. Windows ARM64 application and
server-archive test Clippy passed with warnings denied. Formatting and diff
checks passed. These results do not cover a deployed privileged helper or a
recurring protected-folder job.

### Agent root-bypass option after PR #7

The pinned Java `root=true` shortcut option now reaches the native run. The
Setup page also exposes an explicit per-run automatic-approval choice. It is
false for new runs and is not restored as execution authority from history.
After the independently reviewed environment probe succeeds, it requests
continuation of ordinary and elevated commands in that run. As in Java,
permitted root bypass precedes inline `ask=true`; managed Confirm and the saved
global mutating-command confirmation preference still override root bypass.

The ephemeral grant binds the saved AI configuration and profile revision.
Command, directory, stream, SSH route, sandbox and redaction checks still run.
Background dispatch rereads saved authority. Pause, failed commands, cancellation,
run closure and invalidated grants end the root request. Typed passwordless sudo
uses the existing SSH command route. Typed password sudo requests a separate
choice of vault or manual authentication when necessary and can reuse this run's
matching authenticated sudo terminal. It does not select or submit a vault
password automatically. The authentication controls identify that choice
separately from command approval. Local or otherwise unsupported typed sudo
targets remain blocked.

Grants now share an explicit revocation marker with their background copies.
Removing a grant or dropping its run invalidates those copies. Pausing a run
also advances an outstanding approved-directory epoch, so a delayed directory
reply cannot launch a command after pause/resume. This applies to ordinary and
read-only continuation as well as root bypass. Commands already started retain
the existing cancellation semantics.

### Automatic read-only Agent dispatch and per-run confirmation after PR #7

Agent Run can continue a model-labelled read-only command set after the user
approves the environment probe and that probe succeeds. Every command in the
set must remain ordinary and free of recognized elevation. Java's heredoc and
write-redirection checks promote known mutation shapes to confirmation; native
command-word checks also cover absolute paths, wrapper commands, newlines and
PowerShell file operations. These heuristics are not an OS permission boundary.
An explicit model `needs_confirmation` status promotes command risk even when
the model labels it read-only.

The inline `ask` option now reaches the run instead of being discarded. The
Setup checkbox can also require confirmation for every command in that run.
This mode disables automatic read-only dispatch and future-command grants.
Automatic dispatch retains destination, directory, stream, profile revision,
saved configuration and managed-policy checks. Managed Confirm permits eligible
read-only commands; it still blocks broad grants for mutating commands. The
global mutating-command preference has matching UI text.

The final source passed native Apple Silicon and Fedora ARM64 execution:
242 Agent tests (three ignored), 27 Agent backend tests, 58 Scheduler-Agent
tests and 337 AI Manager tests (12 ignored on macOS, 10 on Fedora). The new
automatic-dispatch and command-shape fixtures and two continuation fixtures
also passed as explicit focused selections. Windows ARM64 application/test
Clippy passed with warnings denied; formatting and diff checks passed. This
is targeted runtime coverage, not a full workspace or live-SSH acceptance run.

### Agent command name migration after PR #7

Java `terminalAgentCommandName` and
`terminalAgentCommandNameCaseInsensitive` now import as independently optional,
inactive AI Manager hints. The reader follows Java's ASCII command character
rules, trims the name and resolves blank names to `agent`. Invalid names,
invalid booleans and names beyond the native input bound are reported as
omitted. Additive replay fills absent hint fields and preserves every native
shortcut preference. Portable backup retains the suggestions.

The AI Manager General page displays the imported name and case setting.
Explicit adoption changes only the specified fields. It preserves the shortcut
enablement switch and requires the normal Save before local and SSH prompt
recognition sees the new settings. Save uses the existing configuration snapshot
check, so a concurrent import cannot be overwritten by a stale dialog.

The former 32-byte native alias limit was narrower than Java's validator.
Rust now accepts aliases up to 8 KiB, with the same ASCII letters, digits,
hyphens and underscores and an initial letter. The input-capture budget now
includes the full alias, prompt and options budgets. Java does not impose this
alias length cap; names above 8 KiB remain an explicit native input limit and
are reported as omitted rather than truncated.

## Scheduler privileged file replacement

Single-file uploads and downloads offer one-use replacement review with
passwordless or vault-backed sudo. Each regular file can be up to 1 GiB.
Review binds the receiver's identity, contents and metadata to the saved action
and pinned SSH route. Upload review checks the local payload and the configured
server replacement scope. The Linux helper streams and verifies the payload
under its protected command and uses the existing native receiver publisher.
The publisher saves the original, confirms authorization before publication
and retains the supported receiver metadata. The Scheduler writes the recovery
path to the journal.

Portable backup restores these jobs disabled with their paths and sudo mode.
Q2 tracks configured deployment and remaining metadata coverage for protected folder merges.

For the download path, native Windows ARM64 and macOS app tests passed approval persistence,
single-use enforcement, local recovery and exact destination checks. Native
macOS and Fedora tests verified portable backup. The final Fedora ARM64 test
build used 26 Cargo jobs and LLD. Its integration exercised both sudo modes
through pinned OpenSSH in a private namespace. The sudo PAM stack checked a
synthetic password. Both routes rejected changed destinations, changed saved
routes and denied transfer policy, then preserved the original's bytes and
the receiver mode on successful publication. The Apple Silicon release ZIP
passed its checksum, native architecture, ad hoc signatures and CLI start
checks.

## Recurring protected Scheduler file replacement

The Scheduler can approve a protected file replacement for a calendar or
Chain on one pinned Linux SSH route. Both directions support passwordless
and vault-backed sudo. The approval binds the literal paths, route, elevation,
time zone and exact triggers. Each firing accepts bounded current source bytes
and requires the reviewed receiver fingerprint. Only a confirmed, held
successor advances the saved receiver. A pending publication survives a
restart and an uncertain outcome requires fresh review. Portable backup
preserves settings and clears the approval on the restored disabled job.

Fedora ARM64 passed real pinned OpenSSH transfers in both directions with
both sudo modes. Two successive firings used different source contents and
retained each original with its supported access metadata. The fixture
rejected oversized sources, replayed firings and an externally changed
receiver. Native Apple Silicon passed the Scheduler and approval-store
regressions and verified the ad hoc signed release ZIP and CLI start.
Windows ARM64 passed strict application Clippy and both recurring replacement
regressions, including native publication on a reviewed private directory.

files and receiver-only entries. Replacements retain supported local access
metadata and keep the originals in private recovery directories. Restored
Java folder download drafts can adopt an existing destination, and portable

## Protected Scheduler folder uploads into existing directories

One-use uploads use an installed Linux helper and the exact saved,
pinned SSH route. The configured destination roots cover creation and the
replacement roots authorize inspection and replacement of existing files.
The review binds the payload digests, receiver file fingerprints, directory
identities and server policy. The helper verifies the private stages before
writing any destination entries. It rechecks authority before each publication.
Missing subtrees publish together, unchanged entries keep their identity, and
each replaced file retains its original and name in a private sibling directory.
The run journal reports confirmed changes and the recovery prefix.

## Native local shell presets

Quick Connect and saved profiles share installed shell choices. The Windows
Git Bash preset resolves a Git for Windows installation and runs its Bash
with `--login -i`. The Cygwin preset resolves a Cygwin Bash installation
with the same startup arguments. WSL availability uses the installed
distributions reported by the native Windows launcher. WSL automatic
integration is set up inside the distribution. Windows sandbox policy
rejects a WSL preset because its Linux process cannot be contained by the
Windows shell sandbox. macOS offers Zsh and Bash, and Linux offers Bash.

The Git Bash toolbar action uses the normal local launch path and managed
policy. It retains the Java icon and resolves the exact action ID. Existing
imported toolbars with an unavailable `toolbar.gitBash` entry obtain the
action in place. The native profile and connection exchange retain the
chosen preset while resolving the program on the current machine.

## Logfile viewer presentation

The native viewer applies the terminal's link and path detection and the
selected bounded highlight set. Find highlights take precedence. Clicks copy
the complete rendered token through the workspace clipboard policy and a
page revision check. Link and keyword switches and the set ID persist in
the profile and can be adopted from Java backups. Additive Java restore
imports custom sets with compatible display rules within the native
catalogue limits. When a local ID has a different definition, an imported
set receives a stable replacement ID and an unset viewer selection uses
that ID. Existing sets, selections, and trigger settings take precedence.
The preview reports unsupported rules and omitted trigger actions.
Unavailable custom sets use the built-in errors and warnings set.
The same mapping resolves live terminal defaults and per-connection
selections in newly imported SSH, local shell and serial profiles. Java's
master switch and alternate-screen choice fill unset fields. An explicit
None stops inheritance, while an unavailable source set falls back to the
global selection. Credential and other transactional restores verify the
mapping before publishing connections. The serial connection editor
offers the same selection as the SSH and local shell editors.
Imported highlight rules and Quick Select patterns retain Java syntax.
The bounded matcher supports Java literal quoting, named captures,
ASCII word boundaries, Unicode character classes, supported Unicode
categories, line-break sequences and final-line anchors. The latter
exclude the terminator from copied or styled ranges. Journal marker
rules also use the shared translation. Lookarounds, numeric and named
backreferences, atomic groups and possessive quantifiers use the bounded
Rust matcher already linked for tokenization. Numeric references follow
Java's group numbering and retain trailing literal digits when applicable.
Named and numeric backreferences apply the ASCII or Unicode case folding
in effect at each reference. Unicode backreferences use the JDK 25 simple
case comparison from Unicode 16.0 and support equivalent characters with
different UTF-8 widths.
Large input and expressions that exceed the evaluation limits may produce
no match. Journal rules retain their original priority when they use
different matchers. Java inline and scoped case, Unicode-class, dot-all,
multiline, Unix-lines and comments settings are restored, including
changes within a group. Comments mode preserves escaped and quoted text
and applies Java's whitespace rules to classes, repetitions and escapes.
Java patterns support extended graphemes and the boundary check relative
to the previous match. The opt-in instructions use the native Unicode
segmentation tables and have a per-search work limit. The tables implement
Unicode 17, while the reference application's default JDK 25 uses Unicode
16 for grapheme segmentation. Supported Unicode case-insensitive bracket
classes use Java's singleton and range rules. The translator expands
class members before applying negation and preserves the configured
shorthand and category predicates. Unicode-aware literals use Java's
distinct rules for a single character and a contiguous run. The
translator preserves those boundaries across quoting and escapes,
and separates the final character of a run when a quantifier applies.
Nested bracket classes and intersections preserve the order of union,
intersection, and whole-class negation. All 18 Java-named character
properties use the matcher's Unicode 16.0 tables and Java-specific
identifier and whitespace rules. POSIX properties use ASCII by default
and Unicode with the Java Unicode-character-class flag. Java binary
Unicode properties, category aliases, and explicit category selectors
are also recognized. Script and block selectors distinguish Unicode
script membership from block ranges. Octal and control escapes, paired
UTF-16 escapes and short Unicode category escapes are supported. The
bounded matcher uses Java's previous-match end for `\G` and retains an
empty match directly after a nonempty match. Short script aliases and Java's
historical block names come from the Unicode 16.0 catalog with verified
Java-specific aliases. Java's handling of missing intersection operands
and lone ampersands after nested intersection operands remains open, as
does visible desktop interaction.

The comparison also reproduced a general `regex-syntax` 0.8.11 negation
issue at U+D7FF and U+E000. Negating the union of `Cn` and `Co` through
bracket syntax erroneously includes these characters. Imported Java
character classes and property complements now subtract the positive

set operations. The surrogate category has an empty scalar set.

The Java grapheme matcher uses the Unicode 16.0 classifications
observed in OpenJDK 25.0.2. It applies Java's control rules for
unassigned scalars and its cluster rules for pictographic sequences
following Prepend characters. The comparison through the Rust
application matcher reproduced OpenJDK's match boundaries for
`\X`, `\b{g}` and `\b{g}\X` over 24,344 scalar strings. It
included the Unicode 16.0 and 17.0 GraphemeBreakTest inputs, products

inside a character is reported at its beginning.
